keyIdea:
An angle measures an amount of turn in degrees. Estimate first (acute $< 90^\circ$, right $= 90^\circ$, obtuse between $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$, reflex $> 180^\circ$), then measure with a protractor, reading from the scale that starts at 0 on one arm.

**Facts (always quote the reason):**
* Angles on a straight line add up to $180^\circ$.
* Angles around a point add up to $360^\circ$.
* Vertically opposite angles are equal.
* Angles in a triangle add up to $180^\circ$.
* An isosceles triangle has two equal sides, and the base angles opposite them are equal.
* The **exterior angle** of a triangle (made by extending one side) equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles, because both make $180^\circ$ with the third interior angle.

Two angles adding to $90^\circ$ are complementary; two adding to $180^\circ$ are supplementary (US terms). When angles are given in algebra, form an equation from a fact, solve it, then substitute back.
